title: JSON, Avro, Protobuf and the schema registry
summary: How the three formats trade size, typing and tooling, how a schema registry frames messages, and what each compatibility mode lets you change.

steps.title: Three formats, three trade-offs
body: The same `OrderPlaced` event in each format:
// Avro schema (the reader needs the WRITER's schema to decode the bytes)
// Protobuf (.proto): field NUMBERS are the identity on the wire
| On the wire | text with every field name | binary, **no names or tags** | binary with field numbers |
| `{"orderId":"o-88213","totalCents":1299,"currency":"EUR"}` | about 60 bytes | about 15 bytes | about 17 bytes |
| Read without a schema? | yes | **no**: needs the writer's schema | partly: unknown fields are skipped, names unknown |
| Typing | weak (numbers are doubles in JavaScript; no int64, no decimal) | strong, with unions and defaults | strong; proto3 scalars have no presence unless `optional` |
| Codegen in .NET | optional (`System.Text.Json`) | `Apache.Avro` + `avrogen`, or generic records | `Google.Protobuf` + `Grpc.Tools` (protoc) at build time |
| Usual home | webhooks, low-volume events, public APIs | Kafka with a schema registry | gRPC, Kafka, polyglot teams |
JSON wins on "anyone can read it with `jq`". Binary formats win on size, CPU and an enforced contract.

steps.prompt: A consumer receives an Avro-encoded record but cannot reach the schema it was written with. What can it do?
options: Almost nothing reliable: Avro binary has no field names or tags, so the bytes only make sense with the writer's schema
Decode it with its own reader schema; Avro matches fields by name in the bytes
Skip unknown fields the way Protobuf does
explain: That is exactly why Avro on Kafka travels with a schema registry: each message carries the writer schema's **id**,
and the consumer fetches (and caches) the schema by id, then resolves it against its own reader schema.

steps.prompt: Complete the Avro fields so old records (written before these fields existed) can still be read.
explain: A reader schema field with a `default` can read data that lacks it. For an optional value use a union with `null`
**first**, because an Avro union's default must match the union's first branch.

steps.title: The schema registry and compatibility modes
body: A **schema registry** (Confluent Schema Registry, Apicurio, Azure Event Hubs schema registry, AWS Glue Schema
Registry) stores versions of each schema under a **subject** and gives each schema a global **id**.
(`shop.orders.OrderPlaced`) allows several event types on one topic.
- The Confluent wire format puts 5 bytes in front of every payload:
Before registering a new version the registry checks it against the subject's **compatibility mode**:
| `BACKWARD` (default) | the new schema can read data written with the previous one | **consumers** |
| `FORWARD` | data written with the new schema can be read with the previous one | **producers** |
| `*_TRANSITIVE` | the same, against **every** earlier version, not only the latest | as above |
| `NONE` | no check | you are on your own |
Kafka keeps old records, and consumers replay them. That is why `BACKWARD` is the default, and why
`BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE` is the safer choice for topics you replay from the beginning.

steps.prompt: A consumer inspects the first bytes of a record. What does this print?
explain: `0x0000012A` is 298. When a consumer logs "Unknown magic byte!" it is reading bytes that were not produced by a
registry serializer: a plain JSON producer on the same topic, or the wrong deserializer.

steps.prompt: For each compatibility mode, which side should you deploy first when you change the schema?
explain: BACKWARD: the **new reader** handles old data, so new consumers can go out while old producers still write the old
shape. FORWARD: **old readers** handle new data, so producers can go first. FULL gives you both.

steps.title: Can this reader read that writer?
prompt: Model a record schema as a list of fields. The tests define:
record Field(string Name, string Type, bool HasDefault);
Write `bool CanRead(List<Field> reader, List<Field> writer)`: can a consumer using the `reader` schema decode data
written with the `writer` schema? Use Avro's resolution rules, simplified:
- every reader field must either exist in the writer with the **same name and type**, or (if the writer does not
- one type promotion is allowed: writer `int`, reader `long`;
- writer fields the reader does not know are **ignored**.
solution: if (!r.HasDefault) return false;   // the reader needs a value the writer never wrote
return true;                               // writer fields the reader does not know are skipped
hints: Loop over the reader's fields and look each one up by name in the writer.
Missing in the writer: OK only if `HasDefault`. Present: types equal, or writer `int` and reader `long`.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoV1 = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "int", false) };
var dojoV2 = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "int", false), new("currency", "string", true) };
var dojoNeedsChannel = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "int", false), new("channel", "string", false) };
var dojoTotalLong = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "long", false) };
var dojoTotalString = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "string", false) };
var dojoRenamed = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("amount", "int", false) };
Dojo.Eq("same schema", true, CanRead(dojoV1, dojoV1));
Dojo.Eq("new reader with a defaulted field reads old data", true, CanRead(dojoV2, dojoV1));
Dojo.Eq("old reader ignores the new field", true, CanRead(dojoV1, dojoV2));
Dojo.Eq("new required field cannot be filled from old data", false, CanRead(dojoNeedsChannel, dojoV1));
Dojo.Eq("int written, long read: promotion", true, CanRead(dojoTotalLong, dojoV1));
Dojo.Eq("long written, int read: no", false, CanRead(dojoV1, dojoTotalLong));
Dojo.Eq("int to string: no", false, CanRead(dojoTotalString, dojoV1));
Dojo.Eq("a rename is a remove plus an add", false, CanRead(dojoRenamed, dojoV1));
record Field(string Name, string Type, bool HasDefault);

steps.title: A compatibility checker
prompt: Now the registry's check. Write `string Check(string mode, List<List<Field>> history, List<Field> candidate)`:
- `history` holds the registered versions, oldest first (`history[0]` is version 1).
- `mode` is `BACKWARD`, `FORWARD`, `FULL`, `NONE`, or one of the first three with `_TRANSITIVE`.
- Without `_TRANSITIVE`, `old` is only the latest version; with it, every version, checked **from the newest
- Return `"compatible"`, or `"incompatible with version {n}"` for the first version that fails.
- `NONE`, or an empty history, is always `"compatible"`. An unknown mode throws `ArgumentException`.
Your `CanRead` from the previous step is already in the editor.
starter: if (!r.HasDefault) return false;   // the reader needs a value the writer never wrote
return true;                               // writer fields the reader does not know are skipped

if (baseMode is not ("BACKWARD" or "FORWARD" or "FULL")) throw new ArgumentException($"unknown mode {mode}");
for (int v = history.Count - 1; v >= oldest; v--)
bool ok = baseMode switch { "BACKWARD" => backward, "FORWARD" => forward, _ => backward && forward };
hints: Strip a trailing `_TRANSITIVE` to get the base mode, and remember whether it was there.
Loop `v` from `history.Count - 1` down to `0` (transitive) or only the last index.
`BACKWARD` asks whether the candidate can read old data: `CanRead(candidate, history[v])`.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoV1 = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "int", false) };
var dojoV2 = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "int", false), new("currency", "string", true) };
var dojoHistory = new List<List<Field>> { dojoV1, dojoV2 };
var dojoAddCoupon = new List<Field>(dojoV2) { new("coupon", "string", true) };
var dojoAddRequired = new List<Field>(dojoV2) { new("channel", "string", false) };
var dojoRemoveTotal = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("currency", "string", true) };
var dojoCurrencyRequired = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "int", false), new("currency", "string", false) };
Dojo.Eq("optional field with a default passes FULL", "compatible", Check("FULL", dojoHistory, dojoAddCoupon));
Dojo.Eq("new required field fails BACKWARD", "incompatible with version 2", Check("BACKWARD", dojoHistory, dojoAddRequired));
Dojo.Eq("new required field passes FORWARD", "compatible", Check("FORWARD", dojoHistory, dojoAddRequired));
Dojo.Eq("removing a required field passes BACKWARD", "compatible", Check("BACKWARD", dojoHistory, dojoRemoveTotal));
Dojo.Eq("removing a required field fails FORWARD", "incompatible with version 2", Check("FORWARD", dojoHistory, dojoRemoveTotal));
Dojo.Eq("dropping a default passes BACKWARD against v2 only", "compatible", Check("BACKWARD", dojoHistory, dojoCurrencyRequired));
Dojo.Eq("...but not BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE: v1 has no currency", "incompatible with version 1", Check("BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE", dojoHistory, dojoCurrencyRequired));
Dojo.Eq("NONE accepts anything", "compatible", Check("NONE", dojoHistory, dojoRemoveTotal));
Dojo.Eq("the first version of a subject", "compatible", Check("BACKWARD", new List<List<Field>>(), dojoV1));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("unknown mode", () => Check("SIDEWAYS", dojoHistory, dojoV2));
record Field(string Name, string Type, bool HasDefault);
